method: Built-in imagegen created sixteen temporal poses per asset from text only; FFmpeg crops and sequences those poses. Choppy frame animation, not AI video generation.
rights_note: Generated from original text prompts with no imported footage, reference images, known characters or requested real-person likenesses. OpenAI terms assign output rights as between user and OpenAI to the extent permitted by law, but do not guarantee uniqueness or non-infringement. No Tenor asset license dependency introduced. Not a zero-risk legal clearance or public-domain dedication.
scope: Three initial original GIF experiments; existing 25 samples preserved.

candidates.title: I checked. Still outside.
candidates.prompt: Create a SINGLE animation sprite sheet, 4 columns by 4 rows, exactly sixteen equal square frames in a 1024x1024 image, edge-to-edge tiles, NO gutters, NO borders, NO labels or text. Each tile is the next animation frame read left to right then top to bottom, fixed camera and identical scene composition and character proportions throughout. It will be cut into sixteen separate frames and played as a GIF. Original photorealistic lo-fi phone-camera action, NOT illustration, NOT polished advertising. Flat domestic light, modest grain. A goofy ordinary ginger domestic cat sits in a small unbranded cardboard box on a beige apartment floor; plain wall behind. Entire cat and box visible in each square. Frame 1-3 cat sitting calmly upright with front paws resting inside box, eyes forward. Frame 4-6 cat slowly lowers head and shoulders into box, hindquarters stay planted. Frame 7-9 head dips fully below top edge, only ears barely visible, box same position. Frame 10-12 cat springs head and shoulders up suddenly with big startled eyes and both forepaws on the rim. Frame 13-16 cat freezes upright staring awkwardly directly at camera, one ear slightly folded. Each adjacent frame has a small real pose change within these beats; this is temporal motion, not sixteen variants. Same cat markings, exact box and room throughout. No identifiable people, branded objects, known meme characters, borrowed footage, watermark, subtitles or readable writing. Joke is an ordinary cat hiding then immediately regretting it. Keep framing unglamorous and a little too low.
interpretations: I checked and immediately regretted it.
I am hiding from a tiny responsibility.

candidates.title: Coffee in theory.
candidates.prompt: Generate ONE 1024x1024 animation sprite sheet with EXACTLY 4 columns and 4 rows = 16 equal square frames. No spacing, no gutters, no panel outlines, no numbers or text. Frames read left to right then top to bottom and will be played consecutively as a GIF. Fixed camera: photorealistic rough compressed phone snapshot of one entirely fictional ordinary adult man with short curly hair and a plain dark green T-shirt, sitting at a cheap kitchen table, waist-up. Neutral wall, unbranded mug stationary on the table at lower left. Flat natural light, slightly awkward crop, NOT cinematic, NOT illustrated. SAME man and identical kitchen in every frame, no camera movement. Silent comic action: Frames 1-3 he has his right hand relaxed on the table near but NOT touching the mug, his eyes distractedly look left. Frames 4-6 he raises his EMPTY right hand with thumb and fingers curled as though holding a mug, toward his mouth; the real mug stays visibly on the table. Frames 7-9 he purses his lips and tilts the empty hand at his mouth as if sipping. Frames 10-12 he stops, slowly shifts his eyes down to the empty hand with an embarrassed puzzled expression. Frames 13-16 he lowers his empty hand slightly and stares deadpan at camera, actual mug still visible untouched on the table. Real progressive arm, face and eye movement; not static variants. No real people's likeness, no celebrity, no existing meme recreation, logos, watermark, text or brand. Each square is a complete aligned animation frame; keep face, body, background and mug coherent throughout. Understated tired-morning humor.
interpretations: My routine started before my brain.
I am pretending this is enough.

candidates.title: I was fixing my hair.
candidates.prompt: Produce one 1024x1024 sprite sheet for a photorealistic stop-motion GIF: EXACTLY 16 equally sized SQUARE frames, 4 columns by 4 rows, edge to edge with ZERO gutters, no frame numbers, no writing, no drawn borders. Read rows left to right. Same fixed phone-camera composition throughout, medium waist-up framing of an entirely fictional young adult woman with short dark bob hair, wearing an unbranded loose blue sweatshirt, in an ordinary apartment hallway with plain cream wall and door. Flat overhead domestic light, slightly grainy low-fidelity candid footage style, no cinematic polish, no illustration. Genuine temporal sequence: frame 1-2 looks just past camera with neutral expression, both hands down. Frame 3-4 hopeful recognition, right elbow begins lifting. Frame 5-7 right open hand rises beside her head and waves once enthusiastically; eyes brighten. Frame 8-9 smile suddenly disappears as she realizes the greeting wasn't meant for her; open hand freezes awkwardly midair beside her ear. Frame 10-12 the raised hand slowly turns and goes to the back of her head, disguising the wave as a hair adjustment. Frame 13-14 she scratches the back of her head with embarrassed lips pressed tight, glancing away. Frame 15-16 hand lowers, looks down pretending nothing happened. Each tile must contain visibly progressing action with consistent face, hands, clothing, background and camera scale. No actual real person, recognizable character, logos, watermarks, branded objects or readable text. The comedy is social awkwardness and the abrupt deadpan pause, readable silently.
interpretations: I am recovering from a social mistake.
I changed my mind halfway through.
